free_tier.stated: 'Our Open Source plan includes: 10,000 credits per month, Free production deploys, Unlimited team members, Sites remain active even if credits run out'. Available to a project that holds an OSI licence, publishes a Code of Conduct, and links back to Netlify.

egress.terms: No separate bandwidth allowance: bandwidth draws on the monthly credit pool of 10,000 credits at 20 credits per GB (derived: 10,000 / 20 = 500 GB if the whole pool is spent on bandwidth). Overage: extra credits are sold at the Pro plan rate, $0.13 per GB of bandwidth.

interface_detail: REST API and CLI documented at docs.netlify.com; no SSH access to a machine is documented.
tooling: the provider documents its own CLI, per the Netlify CLI page: "Netlify's command line interface (CLI)"
chaining: Build minutes and functions are the cheapest place to run a scheduled job that wakes a rented GPU host and kills it again, which is exactly the control plane a no-budget workload needs.

limits.value: A review of the application decides entry, and the site must carry a visible Netlify badge; the credit is monthly and does not roll over.

notes: The best-documented small vendor credit: the number, the renewal rule and the durability term are all printed. The one structural catch is the badge requirement, which puts a vendor link on the project's front page.
